title: "White Space: The Most Underused Tool in PowerPoint" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: White Space: PowerPoint's Most Underused Tool
slides.notes: Most people see empty room on a slide and fill it. That instinct makes slides harder to read. Here's how white space fixes it.

slides.title: White space guides the eye
bullets: Focus: one element in open space
slides.notes: White space is any area without content, not just white. It focuses the eye, groups related things with gaps, and makes a slide feel calm and confident.

slides.title: Find space in a crowded deck
bullets: Group with gaps, align to a few lines
slides.notes: Delete repeated logos and decorative shapes first. Then move reminders into your speaker notes, the single biggest source of new space in most decks.

slides.title: The slide carries less but says more
bullets: Before: seven bullets, two logos, squeezed chart
After: "New customers doubled after we simplified sign-up"
"Sign-up went from five steps to two"
slides.notes: The before slide had seven bullets, two logos and a tiny chart. The after slide has one point, one big chart and one supporting line.

slides.title: Space matters more in video
bullets: Viewers can't lean closer or flip back
Clean slides stay crisp when compressed
Keep the bottom clear for captions
slides.notes: In a video, viewers can't lean in or flip back. Spacious slides stay crisp, give animation room to work, and leave the bottom clear for captions.

slides.title: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out
bullets: On Pro, a.i. directs each animated scene
slides.notes: Your speaker notes become the narration. On Pro, a.i. turns uncluttered slides into calm animated scenes. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
